title: Handoff-Guard: Evidence-backed signoffs and operator handoff for model promotions
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background: As we expand canary/A-B/shadow rollout tooling, customers need deterministic, auditable signoffs and clear operator handoffs for model promotions. This ticket captures a product spec to add an evidence-backed signoff flow (Handoff-Guard) that ties RBAC, timeboxed approvals, and immutable audit bundles to model promotion actions (canary weight increases, full promotion, auto-rollback triggers).

Goal: Ship a product-quality approval workflow that: (1) requires configurable signatories before promotion beyond configured canary thresholds, (2) emits complete audit bundles (metadata, evaluation snapshots, sample inference traces, metric deltas), (3) integrates with RBAC so only authorized roles can approve, (4) supports timeboxed approvals with automatic expiration, (5) hooks into auto-rollback so approvals are recorded before automated policy actions, and (6) surfaces evidence inline in Console and via API for downstream compliance workflows.
acceptance_criteria: Console: 'Promotion requires signoff' toggle exists and is persisted per environment/route.
RBAC: Only users in roles with 'can_promote' permission can approve; attempts by unauthorized users produce 403 and recorded audit event.

Audit bundle: Promotion audit bundle contains model version, canary configuration, signed evaluation snapshot link, top-k inference samples, metric diffs, approver metadata, timestamp, and approval TTL.
API: /promotions endpoints return current approval state and link to audit bundle; clients can attach evidence via pre-signed upload URL.
Timeboxed approvals: Approval entries expire after configured TTL and cannot be used to promote after expiry; Console shows remaining TTL.
Auto-rollback compatibility: If a promotion is auto-rolled back by policy, audit bundle contains the rollback evidence and references approving signoffs.
End-to-end test: E2E run demonstrates a canary promotion blocked until two signoffs, approvers recorded, bundle retrievable, and promotion proceeds when signoffs present.
design_decisions: Attach evidence as an immutable object stored in S3 with checksum; UI shows preview and a download link.
Use existing RBAC roles and add granular permission 'can_promote:model' to avoid new role proliferation.
Leverage current rollout state machine; insert a 'pending_signoffs' state that aborts ephemeral autoscaling changes until approvals are satisfied.
Store approval records in the change ledger (append-only, tamper-evident) to simplify forensic audits.
Approval TTL defaults to 72 hours but is configurable per project.
implementation_notes: Backend: Add signoff table with fields: promotion_id, approver_id, timestamp, evidence_key, ttl, comment. Emit audit event 'promotion.signoff' on success.
Runtime: Ensure canary weight shifts are gated by approval state; add fast-path for 'emergency override' if user has 'can_override_promotion' permission (audit logged).
API: New endpoints: POST /promotions/:id/signoffs, GET /promotions/:id/audit-bundle, DELETE /promotions/:id/signoffs/:signoff_id for revocation by approver within TTL.
Console: Approval drawer UI with list of required signatories, evidence attachments, and Approve/Request Changes actions.
test_plan: Unit tests for signoff lifecycle, permission checks, TTL behavior.
Integration tests: promotion blocked without signoff, passes with required signoffs, expired signoff is rejected.
Chaos test: Simulate partial failures during evidence upload to ensure promotion remains pending and retries are idempotent.
Security test: Verify audit bundle is immutable and KMS-encrypted; verify RBAC prevents unauthorized approvals.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Beta): Enable feature for 10 internal customers and Redwood self-hosted instances. Gather feedback on evidence size and UI clarity.
Phase 2: Expose to all hosted projects as opt-in configuration; default off for existing customers.
Phase 3: Default-on for new projects after 6 weeks of Beta with no critical issues; announce in release notes and Docs.
Migration: Existing promotion configs retained; projects must opt-in to require signoffs.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Evidence bundles grow large and increase storage costs. Mitigation: enforce size limits and provide summarized thumbnails; archive older bundles to infrequent storage class.
Risk: Added approval step increases time-to-promotion and may impact SLOs. Mitigation: allow emergency override with strict audit and require two-person approval for high-impact promotions.
Risk: Complex RBAC changes introduce regressions. Mitigation: staged rollout with feature flag and targeted integration tests.
